verses.text: Hear di word wey di Lord speak to una, house of Israel.
Di Lord talk like dis: “No learn di way of di nations, and no dey dismayed at di signs of heaven, because di nations dey dismayed at dem.
Because di customs of di peoples na vanity. Because one dey cut tree out of di forest, di work of di hands of di craftsman with di axe.
Dem decorate am with silver and with gold. Dem fasten am with nails and with hammers, so that e no go move.
Dem be like scarecrow for cucumber field, and no fit speak. Dem must dey carried, because dem no fit waka. No fear dem, because dem no fit do evil, neither dey in dem to do good.”
Dey none like you, di Lord. You great, and your name great for might.
Who no go fear you, King of di nations? Because dis na your due. Because among all di wise men of di nations, and for all dem kingdoms, dey none like you.
But dem dey altogether brutish and foolish, di instruction of idols, wey na only wood.
Silver beaten into plates dey brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, di work of di craftsman and of di hands of di goldsmith. Blue and purple na dem clothing. Dem all na work of skilful men.
But di Lord na di true God. E na di living God, and everlasting King. At im wrath di earth tremble, and di nations no fit endure im indignation.
Dem go talk to dem like dis: “Di gods wey no make di heavens and di earth, dem go perish from di earth, and from under di heavens.”
E don make di earth by im power. E don establish di world by im wisdom, and by im understanding e don stretch out di heavens.
When e utter im voice, tumult of waters dey for di heavens, and e cause di clouds to ascend from di ends of di earth. E make lightnings with di rain, and bring out di wind from im storehouses.
Every man dey brutish, without knowledge. Every goldsmith dey disgraced by im engraved image, because im molten image na falsehood, and no breath dey inside dem.
Dem na vanity, work of delusion. For di time of dem visitation dem go perish.
Di Portion of Jacob no be like dem, because e na di Maker of all things, and Israel na di tribe of im inheritance. Di Lord of Armies na im name.
Gather up your wares out of di land, you wey dwell under siege.
Because di Lord talk like dis: “See, I go sling out di inhabitants of di land at dis time, and I go bring distress on dem, so that dem go find am.”
Woe to me because of my hurt! My wound dey grievous. But I talk, “Truly dis na grief, and I must bear am.”
My tent don destroy, and all my cords dey broken. My children don go from me, and dem no dey. Nobody dey to stretch out my tent again, and to set up my curtains.
Because di shepherds don become brutish, and no seek di Lord. Therefore dem no prosper, and all dem flocks dey scattered.
Di sound of report! See, e don come, and great commotion out of di north country, to make di cities of Judah desolate, den of jackals.
Di Lord, I know say man way no dey for imself. E no dey for man wey waka to direct im steps.
Di Lord, correct me, but with justice, no with your anger, lest you bring me to nothing.
Pour out your wrath on di nations wey no know you, and on di families wey no call on your name, because dem don devour Jacob. Yes, dem don devour am, and consume am, and don lay waste im habitation.
Di word wey come to Jeremiah from di Lord, say,
“Hear di words of dis covenant, and speak to di men of Judah and to di inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Talk to dem, ‘Di Lord, di God of Israel, talk like dis: Cursed be di man wey no obey di words of dis covenant,

wey I command una fathers for di day wey I bring dem out of di land of Egypt, out of di iron furnace, saying, “Obey my voice, and do dem, according to all wey I command una. So una go be my people, and I go be una God,”
so that I go perform di oath wey I swear to una fathers, to give dem land flowing with milk and honey, as e dey dis day.’” Den I answer, “Amen, di Lord.”
Di Lord talk to me, “Proclaim all dis words for di cities of Judah and for di streets of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Hear di words of dis covenant, and do dem.
Because I earnestly testify to una fathers for di day wey I bring dem up out of di land of Egypt, even to dis day, rising early and testifying, saying, “Obey my voice.”
Yet dem no obey, nor incline dem ear, but everyone waka for di stubbornness of dem evil heart. Therefore I bring on dem all di words of dis covenant, wey I command dem to do, but dem no do.’”
Di Lord talk to me, “Conspiracy dey found among di men of Judah and among di inhabitants of Jerusalem.

Dem don turn back to di iniquities of dem forefathers, wey refuse to hear my words. Dem don go after other gods to serve dem. Di house of Israel and di house of Judah don break my covenant wey I make with dem fathers.
Therefore di Lord talk like dis: ‘See, I go bring evil on dem, wey dem no go fit escape. Dem go cry to me, but I no go listen to dem.
Den di cities of Judah and di inhabitants of Jerusalem go go and cry to di gods to whom dem burn incense, but dem no go save dem at all for di time of dem trouble.
Because according to di number of your cities na your gods, Judah. According to di number of di streets of Jerusalem don una set up altars to di shameful thing, altars to burn incense to Baal.’
Therefore no pray for dis people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for dem, because I no go hear for di time wey dem cry to me because of dem trouble.
Wetin my beloved dey do for my house, seeing say she don work lewdness with many? Di consecrated flesh fit take away your evil? Den you go rejoice.
Di Lord call your name ‘Green olive tree, beautiful with goodly fruit.’ With di noise of great tumult e don kindle fire on am, and im branches dey broken.

Because di Lord of Armies, wey plant you, don pronounce evil against you, because of di evil of di house of Israel and of di house of Judah, wey dem don do against demselves to provoke me to anger by burning incense to Baal.”
Di Lord don make me know am, and I know am. Den you show me dem doings.

But I be like gentle lamb wey dem dey lead to di slaughter. I no know say dem don devise devices against me, saying, “Make we destroy di tree with im fruit, and make we cut am off from di land of di living, so that im name no go dey remembered again.”
But, di Lord of Armies, wey judge righteously, wey try di heart and di mind, make I see your vengeance on dem, because to you I don reveal my cause.
Therefore di Lord talk like dis concerning di men of Anathoth, wey seek your life, saying, “No prophesy for di name of di Lord, so that you no go die by our hand.”
Therefore di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “See, I go punish dem. Di young men go die by di sword. Dem sons and dem daughters go die by famine.
No remnant go remain to dem, because I go bring evil on di men of Anathoth, even di year of dem visitation.”
Righteous you dey, di Lord, when I contend with you, but yet I go talk with you about justice. Why di way of di wicked dey prosper? Why dem dey at ease wey deal very treacherously?
You don plant dem. Yes, dem don take root. Dem grow. Yes, dem bring forth fruit. You dey near for dem mouth, and far from dem heart.
But you, di Lord, know me. You see me, and test my heart toward you. Pull dem out like sheep for slaughter, and prepare dem for di day of slaughter.
How long di land go mourn, and di herbs of every field wither? For di wickedness of dem wey dwell inside am, di animals and di birds dey consumed, because dem talk, “E no go see our last end.”
“If you don run with di footmen, and dem don weary you, den how you go compete with horses? Though for land of peace you dey safe, but how you go do for di thicket of di Jordan?
Because even your brothers and di house of your father, even dem don deal treacherously with you. Even dem don cry aloud after you. No believe dem, though dem speak good words to you.
I don forsake my house. I don cast off my heritage. I don give di dearly beloved of my soul into di hand of her enemies.
My heritage don become to me like lion for di forest. E don lift up im voice against me. Therefore I hate am.
My heritage no dey to me like speckled bird of prey? Di birds of prey dey against am all round? Go, assemble all di animals of di field. Bring dem to devour.
Many shepherds don destroy my vineyard. Dem don trample my portion under foot. Dem don make my pleasant portion desolate wilderness.
Dem don make am desolate. Desolate, e mourn to me. Di whole land don dey made desolate, because no man lay am to heart.
Destroyers don come on all di bare heights for di wilderness, because di sword of di Lord devour from one end of di land even to di other end of di land. No flesh get peace.
Dem don sow wheat, and don reap thorns. Dem don exhaust demselves, but no profit. Dem go dey ashamed of una harvests because of di fierce anger of di Lord.”

Di Lord talk like dis against all my evil neighbours, wey touch di inheritance wey I don cause my people Israel to inherit: “See, I go pluck dem up from off dem land, and I go pluck up di house of Judah from among dem.
E go happen, after I don pluck dem up, I go return and have compassion on dem. I go bring dem again, every man to im heritage, and every man to im land.
E go happen, if dem go diligently learn di ways of my people, to swear by my name, ‘As di Lord live,’ even as dem teach my people to swear by Baal, den dem go dey built up among my people.
But if dem no obey, den I go pluck up dat nation, plucking up and destroying am,” talk di Lord.
Di Lord talk like dis to me: “Go, and buy yourself linen belt, and put am on your waist, and no put am in water.”
So I buy belt according to di word of di Lord, and put am on my waist.
Di word of di Lord come to me di second time, say,
“Take di belt wey you don buy, wey dey on your waist, and arise, go to di Euphrates, and hide am dere for hole of di rock.”
So I go, and hide am by di Euphrates, as di Lord command me.
After many days, di Lord talk to me, “Arise, go to di Euphrates, and take from dere di belt wey I command you to hide dere.”
Den I go to di Euphrates, and dig, and take di belt from di place where I hide am. See, di belt don spoil. E no good for anything.
Den di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Di Lord talk like dis: ‘Even so I go spoil di pride of Judah, and di great pride of Jerusalem.
Dis evil people, wey refuse to hear my words, wey waka for di stubbornness of dem heart, and go after other gods to serve dem, and to worship dem, go be even as dis belt, wey no good for anything.

Because as di belt cling to di waist of man, so I don cause di whole house of Israel and di whole house of Judah to cling to me,’ talk di Lord, ‘so that dem go be to me for people, and for name, and for praise, and for glory. But dem no listen.’
Therefore you go speak to dem dis word: ‘Di Lord, di God of Israel, talk like dis: Every bottle go dey filled with wine.’ Dem go talk to you, ‘We no know say every bottle go dey filled with wine?’

Den you go talk to dem, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: See, I go fill all di inhabitants of dis land, even di kings wey sit on David throne, and di priests, and di prophets, and all di inhabitants of Jerusalem, with drunkenness.
I go dash dem one against another, even di fathers and di sons together,’ talk di Lord. ‘I no go pity, nor spare, nor have compassion, but destroy dem.’”
Hear, and give ear. No dey proud, because di Lord don speak.

Give glory to di Lord your God, before e cause darkness, and before your feet stumble on di dark mountains, and while una look for light, e turn am into di shadow of death, and make am gross darkness.
But if una no hear am, my soul go weep in secret for your pride. My eye go weep bitterly, and run down with tears, because di Lord flock don dey taken captive.
Talk to di king and to di queen mother, “Humble yourselves. Sit down, because your crowns don fall from your heads, your beautiful crowns.”
Di cities of di South dey shut up, and nobody fit open dem. Judah dey carried away captive, all of am. E dey wholly carried away captive.
Lift up your eyes, and see dem wey dey come from di north. Where di flock wey dem give you, your beautiful flock?
Wetin you go talk when e go set over you as head those wey you don teach to be your friends? No go sorrows take you, like woman for labour?
If you talk for your heart, “Why dis things don come on me?” For di greatness of your iniquity your skirts dey uncovered, and your heels dey violently treated.
Di Ethiopian fit change im skin, or di leopard im spots? Den una go fit do good, wey dey accustomed to do evil.
“Therefore I go scatter dem like stubble wey pass away by di wind of di wilderness.
Dis na your lot, di portion wey I don measure to you,” talk di Lord, “because you don forget me, and trust for falsehood.
Therefore I also go uncover your skirts on your face, and your shame go dey seen.
I don see your abominations, even your adulteries, and your neighings, di lewdness of your prostitution, on di hills for di field. Woe to you, Jerusalem! How long e go dey before you go be clean?”
Di word of di Lord wey come to Jeremiah concerning di drought.
Judah mourn, and her gates languish. Dem sit in black on di ground, and di cry of Jerusalem don go up.
Dem nobles send dem little ones to di waters. Dem come to di cisterns, and find no water. Dem return with dem vessels empty. Dem dey ashamed and confounded, and cover dem heads.
Because di ground dey cracked, because no rain dey for di land, di farmers dey ashamed. Dem cover dem heads.
Yes, even di doe for di field give birth, and leave her young, because no grass dey.
Di wild donkeys stand on di bare heights. Dem pant for di wind like jackals. Dem eyes fail, because no vegetation dey.
Though our iniquities testify against us, do am for your name sake, di Lord, because our backslidings dey many. We don sin against you.
You hope of Israel, im Saviour for time of trouble, why you go be like stranger for di land, and like wayfaring man wey turn aside to stay for night?
Why you go be like man dismayed, like mighty man wey no fit save? Yet you, di Lord, dey among us, and we dey called by your name. No leave us.
Di Lord talk like dis to dis people: “Even so dem don love to wander. Dem no restrain dem feet. Therefore di Lord no accept dem. Now e go remember dem iniquity, and visit dem sins.”
Di Lord talk to me, “No pray for dis people for dem good.
When dem fast, I no go hear dem cry. When dem offer burnt offering and meal offering, I no go accept dem. But I go consume dem by di sword, and by famine, and by pestilence.”
Den I talk, “Ah, Lord God! See, di prophets talk to dem, ‘Una no go see sword, neither una go get famine, but I go give una assured peace for dis place.’”

Den di Lord talk to me, “Di prophets prophesy lies for my name. I no send dem, neither I command dem, neither I speak to dem. Dem prophesy to una false vision, divination, and wetin no dey, and di deceit of dem own heart.

Therefore di Lord talk like dis concerning di prophets wey prophesy for my name, and I no send dem, yet dem talk, ‘Sword and famine no go dey for dis land.’ By sword and famine dem prophets go dey consumed.

Di people to whom dem prophesy go dey cast out for di streets of Jerusalem because of di famine and di sword. Dem no go get person to bury dem, dem, dem wives, dem sons, nor dem daughters. Because I go pour dem wickedness on dem.
You go talk dis word to dem: ‘Make my eyes run down with tears night and day, and no make dem cease, because di virgin daughter of my people don break with great breach, with very grievous wound.

If I go out into di field, den see, those wey dem don kill with di sword. If I enter di city, den see, those wey sick with famine. Yes, both di prophet and di priest go about for di land, and no get knowledge.’”
You don utterly reject Judah? Your soul loathe Zion? Why you don strike us, and no healing dey for us? We look for peace, but no good dey, and for time of healing, and see, terror!
We acknowledge our wickedness, di Lord, and di iniquity of our fathers, because we don sin against you.
No abhor us, for your name sake. No disgrace di throne of your glory. Remember, no break your covenant with us.
Dey any among di vanities of di nations wey fit cause rain? Or di heavens fit give showers? No be you be am, di Lord our God? Therefore we go wait for you, because you don make all dis things.
Den di Lord talk to me, “Though Moses and Samuel stand before me, yet my mind no go dey toward dis people. Cast dem out of my sight, and make dem go out.

E go happen, when dem talk to you, ‘Where we go go?’ den you go tell dem, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: Dem wey dey for death, to death. Dem wey dey for di sword, to di sword. Dem wey dey for famine, to famine. Dem wey dey for captivity, to captivity.’
I go appoint over dem four kinds,” talk di Lord: “di sword to kill, di dogs to tear, di birds of di sky, and di animals of di earth, to devour and to destroy.
I go cause dem to dey tossed to and fro among all di kingdoms of di earth, because of Manasseh, Hezekiah pikin, king of Judah, for wetin e do for Jerusalem.
Because who go have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who go bemoan you? Who go turn aside to ask about your welfare?
You don reject me,” talk di Lord. “You don go backward. Therefore I don stretch out my hand against you, and destroy you. I dey weary with relenting.
I don winnow dem with winnowing fork for di gates of di land. I don bereave dem of children. I don destroy my people. Dem no turn from dem ways.
Dem widows dey increased to me pass di sand of di seas. I don bring on dem, against di mother of di young men, destroyer at noonday. I don cause anguish and terrors to fall on her suddenly.

She wey don bear seven languish. She don give up di spirit. Her sun don set while e still dey day. She don dey disappointed and confounded. Di remnant of dem I go give to di sword before dem enemies,” talk di Lord.
Woe to me, my mother, say you don bear me as man of strife and man of contention to di whole land! I no lend, neither men lend to me, yet everyone curse me.
Di Lord talk, “Surely I go set you free for good. Surely I go cause di enemy make supplication to you for di time of evil and for di time of affliction.
Person fit break iron, iron from di north, and bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I go give for plunder without price, even for all your sins, and for all your borders.
I go make you serve your enemies for di land wey you no know, because fire don dey kindled for my anger, wey go burn on una.”
You know, di Lord. Remember me, and visit me, and avenge me of my persecutors. No take me away for your longsuffering. Know say for your sake I don suffer reproach.
Your words dey found, and I eat dem. Your words dey to me di joy and di rejoicing of my heart, because I dey called by your name, di Lord, di God of Armies.
I no sit for di assembly of dem wey make merry, nor rejoice. I sit alone because of your hand, because you don fill me with indignation.
Why my pain dey perpetual, and my wound incurable, wey refuse to dey healed? You go truly be to me like deceitful brook, like waters wey fail?

Therefore di Lord talk like dis: “If you return, den I go bring you again, and you go stand before me. If you utter wetin precious, and no vile, you go be like my mouth. Dem go return to you, but you no go return to dem.
I go make you to dis people fortified bronze wall. Dem go fight against you, but dem no go prevail against you, because I dey with you to save you and to deliver you,” talk di Lord.
“I go deliver you out of di hand of di wicked, and I go redeem you out of di hand of di terrible.”
Di word of di Lord come also to me, say,
“You no go take wife, neither go get sons or daughters for dis place.”

Because di Lord talk like dis concerning di sons and concerning di daughters wey dem born for dis place, and concerning dem mothers wey bear dem, and concerning dem fathers wey beget dem for dis land:

“Dem go die of grievous deaths. Dem no go dey lamented, neither dem go dey buried. Dem go be as dung on di surface of di ground. Dem go dey consumed by di sword and by famine, and dem dead bodies go be food for di birds of di sky, and for di animals of di earth.”

Because di Lord talk like dis: “No enter di house of mourning, neither go lament nor bemoan dem, because I don take away my peace from dis people,” talk di Lord, “even loving kindness and tender mercies.
Both great and small go die for dis land. Dem no go dey buried. Men no go lament for dem, nor cut demselves, nor make demselves bald for dem.
Men no go break bread for dem for mourning, to comfort dem for di dead. Neither men go give dem di cup of consolation to drink for dem father or for dem mother.
You no go enter di house of feasting to sit with dem, to eat and to drink.

Because di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: See, I go cause to cease from dis place, for una eyes and for una days, di voice of mirth and di voice of gladness, di voice of di bridegroom and di voice of di bride.”

“E go happen, when you go show dis people all dis words, and dem go talk to you, ‘Why di Lord don pronounce all dis great evil against us? Wetin be our iniquity? Wetin be our sin wey we don sin against di Lord our God?’
Den you go talk to dem, ‘Because una fathers don forsake me,’ talk di Lord, ‘and don follow other gods, and don serve dem, and worship dem, and don forsake me, and no keep my law.
Una don do worse pass una fathers, because see, una waka everyone after di stubbornness of im evil heart, so that una no listen to me.
Therefore I go cast una out of dis land into land wey una no know, neither una nor una fathers. Dere una go serve other gods day and night, because I go show una no favour.’”
“Therefore see, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey e no go dey said again, ‘As di Lord live, wey bring up di children of Israel out of di land of Egypt,’
but, ‘As di Lord live, wey bring up di children of Israel from di land of di north, and from all di countries where e don drive dem.’ I go bring dem again into dem land wey I give to dem fathers.

See, I go send for many fishermen,” talk di Lord, “and dem go fish dem. After dat I go send for many hunters, and dem go hunt dem from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of di clefts of di rocks.
Because my eyes dey on all dem ways. Dem no hidden from my face, neither dem iniquity hidden from my eyes.
First I go recompense dem iniquity and dem sin double, because dem don defile my land. Dem don fill my inheritance with di carcasses of dem detestable things and dem abominations.”

Di Lord, my strength and my fortress, and my refuge for di day of affliction, di nations go come to you from di ends of di earth, and go talk, “Our fathers don inherit only lies, vanity and things wherein no profit dey.
Man fit make gods for imself, wey no be gods?”
“Therefore see, I go cause dem to know, dis once I go cause dem to know my hand and my might. Dem go know say my name na di Lord.”
“Di sin of Judah dey written with pen of iron, and with point of diamond. E dey engraved on di tablet of dem heart, and on di horns of una altars,
while dem children remember dem altars and dem Asherah poles by di green trees upon di high hills.
My mountain for di field, I go give your substance and all your treasures for plunder, and your high places for sin, throughout all your borders.
You, even of yourself, go let go of your heritage wey I give you. I go cause you to serve your enemies for di land wey you no know, because una don kindle fire for my anger wey go burn forever.”
Di Lord talk like dis: “Cursed be di man wey trust for man, and make flesh im arm, and whose heart turn away from di Lord.
Because e go be like shrub for di desert, and no go see when good come, but go inhabit di parched places for di wilderness, for salt land wey no dey inhabited.
Blessed be di man wey trust for di Lord, and whose trust di Lord be.

Because e go be like tree planted by di waters, wey spread out im roots by di river, and no go fear when heat come, but im leaf go dey green, and no go dey anxious for year of drought, neither e go cease from yielding fruit.
Di heart dey deceitful above all things, and e dey desperately wicked. Who fit know am?
I, di Lord, search di mind. I try di heart, even to give every man according to im ways, according to di fruit of im doings.
As partridge wey gather young wey e no hatch, so na im wey get riches, but no by right. E go leave dem for di middle of im days, and for im end e go be fool.”
Throne of glory, exalted from di beginning, na di place of our sanctuary.
Di Lord, di hope of Israel, all wey forsake you go dey ashamed. Dem wey depart from me go dey written for di earth, because dem don forsake di Lord, di spring of living waters.
Heal me, di Lord, and I go dey healed. Save me, and I go dey saved, because you na my praise.
See, dem talk to me, “Where di word of di Lord dey? Make am come now.”
As for me, I no hurry away from being shepherd to follow you. Neither I desire di woeful day. You know. Wetin come out of my lips dey before your face.
No be terror to me. You na my refuge for di day of evil.
Make dem dey ashamed wey persecute me, but make me no dey put to shame. Make dem dey dismayed, but make me no dey dismayed. Bring on dem di day of evil, and destroy dem with double destruction.
Di Lord talk like dis to me: “Go, and stand for di gate of di children of di people, by which di kings of Judah come in, and by which dem go out, and for all di gates of Jerusalem,
and talk to dem, ‘Hear di word of di Lord, una kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all di inhabitants of Jerusalem, wey enter by dis gates.
Di Lord talk like dis: Take heed to yourselves, and carry no burden on di Sabbath day, nor bring am in by di gates of Jerusalem.
Neither carry burden out of your houses on di Sabbath day, neither do any work, but make di Sabbath day holy, as I command una fathers.
But dem no listen, nor incline dem ear, but make dem neck stiff, so that dem no go hear, nor receive instruction.
E go happen, if una diligently listen to me,’ talk di Lord, ‘to bring in no burden through di gates of dis city on di Sabbath day, but hallow di Sabbath day, to do no work inside am,

den dere go enter by di gates of dis city kings and princes wey sit on di throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, dem, and dem princes, di men of Judah, and di inhabitants of Jerusalem. Dis city go remain forever.

Dem go come from di cities of Judah, and from di places round about Jerusalem, and from di land of Benjamin, and from di lowland, and from di hill country, and from di South, bringing burnt offerings, sacrifices, meal offerings and frankincense, and bringing sacrifices of thanksgiving, to di house of di Lord.

But if una no listen to me to make di Sabbath day holy, and no to carry burden and enter di gates of Jerusalem on di Sabbath day, den I go kindle fire for im gates, and e go devour di palaces of Jerusalem, and e no go dey quenched.’”
Di word wey come to Jeremiah from di Lord, say,
“Arise, and go down to di potter house, and dere I go cause you to hear my words.”
Den I go down to di potter house, and see, e dey work im work on di wheels.
Di vessel wey e dey make of clay dey marred for di hand of di potter. So e make am again into another vessel, as e seem good to di potter to make am.
Den di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“House of Israel, I no fit do with una as dis potter? Look, as di clay for di potter hand, so una dey for my hand, house of Israel.
One moment I fit speak concerning nation, and concerning kingdom, to pluck up and to break down and to destroy am,
but if dat nation, concerning which I don speak, turn from dem evil, I go relent of di evil wey I think to do to dem.
Another moment I fit speak concerning nation, and concerning kingdom, to build and to plant am,
but if e do evil for my sight, so that e no obey my voice, den I go relent of di good, wey I say I go benefit am.

Now therefore, go talk to di men of Judah, and to di inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: See, I dey frame evil against una, and devise device against una. Return now everyone from im evil way, and make una ways and una doings good.’
But dem talk, ‘Hope no dey. Because we go waka after our own plans, and we go every one do di stubbornness of im evil heart.’”
Therefore di Lord talk like dis: “Ask now among di nations, who don hear such things as dis. Di virgin of Israel don do very horrible thing.
Di snow of Lebanon go fail from di rock of di field? Or di cold flowing waters from far fit dey dried up?
But my people don forget me. Dem don burn incense to vain gods, and dem don stumble for dem ways, for di ancient paths, to waka for paths, for way wey no dey built up,
to make dem land desolate, and permanent hissing. Everyone wey pass by am go dey astonished, and shake im head.
I go scatter dem like with east wind before di enemy. I go show dem di back, and no di face, for di day of dem calamity.”

Den dem talk, “Come, make we devise devices against Jeremiah, because di law no go perish from di priest, nor counsel from di wise, nor di word from di prophet. Come, make we strike am with di tongue, and make we no give heed to any of im words.”
Give heed to me, di Lord, and listen to di voice of dem wey contend with me.
Evil go dey repaid for good? Because dem don dig pit for my soul. Remember say I stand before you to speak good for dem, to turn away your wrath from dem.

Therefore deliver up dem children to di famine, and give dem over to di power of di sword. Make dem wives dey bereaved of dem children, and dey widows. Make dem men dey slain of death, and dem young men dey struck by di sword for battle.
Make cry dey heard from dem houses, when you bring troop suddenly on dem, because dem don dig pit to take me, and hide snares for my feet.

Yet you, di Lord, know all dem counsel against me to kill me. No forgive dem iniquity, neither blot out dem sin from your sight, but make dem dey overthrown before you. Deal with dem for di time of your anger.
Di Lord talk like dis: “Go, and buy potter earthen jar, and take some of di elders of di people and some of di elders of di priests.
Go out to di valley of di son of Hinnom, wey dey di entrance of di gate Harsith, and proclaim dere di words wey I go tell you.

Talk, ‘Hear di word of di Lord, una kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: See, I go bring evil on dis place, wey whoever hear am, im ears go tingle,

because dem don forsake me, and don make dis place strange, and don burn incense inside am to other gods, wey dem no know, dem, and dem fathers, and di kings of Judah. Dem don fill dis place with di blood of innocents,
and don build di high places of Baal, to burn dem sons with fire for burnt offerings to Baal, wey I no command, nor speak, neither e come into my mind.
Therefore see, di days dey come,’ talk di Lord, ‘wey dis place no go dey called Topheth, nor di valley of di son of Hinnom, but di valley of Slaughter.

I go make void di counsel of Judah and Jerusalem for dis place. I go cause dem to fall by di sword before dem enemies, and by di hand of dem wey seek dem life. Dem dead bodies I go give to be food for di birds of di sky and for di animals of di earth.
I go make dis city desolate, and permanent hissing. Everyone wey pass by am go dey astonished and hiss because of all im plagues.

I go cause dem to eat di flesh of dem sons and di flesh of dem daughters, and everyone go eat di flesh of im friend, for di siege and for di distress, wherewith dem enemies, and dem wey seek dem life, go distress dem.’
Den you go break di jar for di sight of di men wey go with you,

and go talk to dem, ‘Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: Even so I go break dis people and dis city, as one break potter vessel, wey no fit dey made whole again. Dem go bury for Topheth, till no place dey to bury.
Na so I go do to dis place,’ talk di Lord, ‘and to di inhabitants of am, even making dis city like Topheth.

Di houses of Jerusalem, and di houses of di kings of Judah, wey dey defiled, go be like di place of Topheth, because of all di houses on whose roofs dem don burn incense to all di army of heaven, and don pour out drink offerings to other gods.’”
Den Jeremiah come from Topheth, where di Lord don send am to prophesy, and e stand for di court of di Lord house, and talk to all di people:

“Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: ‘See, I go bring on dis city and on all im towns all di evil wey I don pronounce against am, because dem don make dem neck stiff, so that dem no go hear my words.’”
